title: How do large language models work?
excerpt: A practical explanation of tokens, training, inference and context windows.
body: Large language models learn statistical relationships between pieces of text called tokens. During training they repeatedly learn to predict missing or next tokens across enormous datasets.
Training produces model parameters that encode useful patterns. During inference, a prompt is processed and the model generates a response token by token.
Context windows determine how much information can be considered at once. More context can help, but good retrieval and prompt design remain important.
